segments.he: אָמְרָה ״קֻוֽנָּם תְּאֵנָה״, אָמַר רָבָא: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא. דְּאָמַר: עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר ״שְׁבוּעָה״ לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
segments.en: The mishna teaches that if a woman «said:» Tasting «a fig» and tasting a grape are «konam» for me, these are viewed as two separate vows. «Rava said: The mishna is» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Shimon, as» Rabbi Shimon «said» that one is not liable to bring multiple offerings for taking false oaths to multiple people in the same utterance, for example, if he says: I take an oath that I do not have your item, nor yours, nor yours, «unless he states» an expression of «an oath to each and every one» of the creditors, for example by stating: I take an oath I do not have yours; I take an oath I do not have yours. Here too, only if she says: Tasting, with respect to each fruit are they viewed as two separate vows.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: מתניתין רבי שמעון היא
moves.summary: identifies the mishna with R' Shimon

moves.cueHe: דאמר: עד שיאמר ״שבועה״ לכל אחד ואחד
moves.summary: R' Shimon: oath term must be said for each

positions.claim: the mishna follows R' Shimon: only repeating the vow term per item makes separate vows
